summary: A weekly low-impact fitness class at Harvest House Community Center, a City of Asheville Parks & Recreation senior center, where participants drum along to music for an arm/core workout. It is a rec-center program alongside Chair Volleyball, Chair Aerobics and Tai Chi, run by Parks & Recreation staff rather than by a self-organized group, with no membership language, named leader, or regular-attendee identity in the listings.

evidence.note: Listing describes a beginner-friendly, no-experience-needed drop-in fitness workout ('Jam to some tunes while getting a great, low-impact arm and core workout') with no mention of members, a roster, or a group identity.

All 8 weekly occurrences share identical boilerplate description text with only the summary lightly reworded, consistent with an auto-generated recurring class listing rather than a community group describing itself.

Web search confirms 'Drumming for Fitness' is one of several lower-impact activities offered at Harvest House alongside Chair Volleyball, Chair Aerobics, and Tai Chi, framed as a program of the senior center, not a standalone drumming community.

The center's official page lists it as one of Asheville Parks and Recreation's fitness/exercise classes (alongside Zumba, yoga, etc.); the only 'membership' mentioned is a voluntary $12 donation to the general Harvest House Association, unrelated to the drumming class specifically.
No Facebook group, Meetup page, Instagram, or dedicated website found for a 'Drumming for Exercise' group at Harvest House.
